I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn, I grow wheat and corn, and that's what the soil here knows. The North China Plain — this is wheat-corn country. I'm 69 now, my back isn't what it was, and I'm not about to start experimenting with something new. My land is about 16 mu. My son lives in the city but comes back for the big harvests when he can.

Winter wheat goes in around October. I'll plant an improved variety — the seed station in town sells Jimai 22 or something similar, I'll ask what they have. I always do three irrigations: one before winter sets in to help the roots, one at jointing, one at heading. I spray twice — once for aphids in spring, once for powdery mildew. I use rotary tillage before planting to break up the soil after summer.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant summer maize right away — no time to waste, you need the full growing season. I go hybrid seed, everyone around here does, the yields are better. Maize gets summer rain so I only irrigate once if it's dry, maybe not at all. I throw down fertilizer at planting and top-dress at the 8-leaf stage. One pesticide spray for armyworm if needed.

I won't try vegetables or cotton — too much bending, too much daily work. Wheat and corn, that's my plan. Hire the machine for plowing and harvesting, do the rest myself.
